newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.N. arms team starts talks in Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.N. arms team starts talks in Iraq.

text.p: A United Nations germ warfare team met Iraqi officials on Sunday to discuss Baghdad's remaining biological weapons, a U.N. arms official said.

Jo Lomas, assistant director of Baghdad's Ongoing Monitoring and Verification Centre, told Reuters the 12-member team arrived on Saturday and met officials from the Iraqi National Monitoring Directorate.

This is the second biological team to arrive in Iraq after the first visit to the county by Richard Butler, head of the U.N. Special Commission (UNSCOM) in charge of disarming Iraq under the 1991 Gulf War ceasefire terms.
Lomas said the biological team, headed by American Dick Sperczec, would stay until Friday. They have not carried any inspection so far, she added.
UNSCOM has often said that Iraq has not revealed all secrets about its past biological warfare capabilities. Baghdad says it has nothing to hide.

Butler, who replaced Sweden's Rolf Ekeus as head of UNSCOM on July 1, said in Baghdad last month that he had agreed with the Iraqis on a plan to eradicate Baghdad's biological, chemical and missile weapons.
"The work agreed between Iraq and the chairman is continuing," Lomas said.

UNSCOM must certify that Iraq has no more weapons of mass destruction before the U.N. Security Council will lift curbs on Iraq's oil exports imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. But the U.N. has allowed Baghdad limited oil sales since last December to buy humanitarian needs for the Iraqis.
